title: Abraham Jacobi opened the first children's clinic in the US and became known as the Father of American Pediatrics

trailer.text: Abraham Jacobi, a German-born physician, is regarded as the Father of American Pediatrics.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, he was imprisoned for his participation in the revolutions of 1848 and fled to America in 1853.

According to a biographical encyclopedia, Jacobi opened the first free clinic for children at the New York Medical College, and according to the journal he was the first to create a free pediatric clinic in the United States.
According to the website Life in the Fast Lane, in 1912 he was elected president of the American Medical Association, and was the first Jew in the role.

stations.title: A poor child from Westphalia, a revolutionary prisoner

paragraphs.text: According to a biographical encyclopedia, he was born into a very poor family.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, in 1851 he received an MD from the University of Bonn.
According to the website, while still a medical student he joined the Communist League, alongside Karl Marx and Carl Schurz.
According to Britannica, he was imprisoned in Berlin and Cologne because he took part in the German revolutionary movement of 1848.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, he spent about two years in chains and solitary confinement, on charges of high treason.
He was acquitted in the Cologne Communist Trial in 1852.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, Abraham Jacobi was born at Hartum, near Minden, Westphalia, on May 6, 1830.
In 1853 he emigrated to the United States, according to two sources.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, he opened a medical practice in New York.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, a year after arriving in New York he invented a laryngoscope.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, Jacobi saw children living and working in substandard and unsafe conditions.
According to the article, ancient medical writings dealt with diseases in children only within general topics.
According to the same article, the first separate children's hospital was founded in Philadelphia in 1855.
According to Britannica, Jacobi became professor of children's diseases at the New York Medical College, holding the first chair in the subject in the United States.
According to the biographical encyclopedia, there he opened the first free clinic for children.
This was the first children's clinic in the United States.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, he was the first to create a free clinic for children in the United States.

stations.title: Mount Sinai: a ward of their own for children

paragraphs.text: According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Jacobi organized the children's ward at Mount Sinai Hospital in New York.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, in 1875 he organized a children's department in the Mount Sinai outpatient dispensary, together with his wife, Mary Putnam Jacobi.
According to the website, in 1879 he established there the first inpatient pediatric ward in New York City.
According to the website, at that time children were usually treated on adult wards, and the ward gave them specialized care.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he was one of the first to insist on the boiling of milk.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, he worked to provide pasteurized milk to babies who could not breastfeed.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he was one of the first to insert a tube into the throat (intubation) instead of operating on the windpipe (tracheotomy).
According to the biographical encyclopedia, in 1870 he returned to the College of Physicians and Surgeons, where he taught for 32 years.

stations.title: The physician who would not accept the slums

paragraphs.text: According to the biographical encyclopedia, other physicians advised tuberculosis patients in the slums to sleep with their heads on the fire escapes.
According to the same source, Jacobi asked why these slums must be tolerated.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, he argued that children's health must be improved through systemic changes: in sanitation, housing, nutrition and education.
According to the website, he denounced large-scale institutional care for orphans.
According to the website, he urged physicians to serve on school boards, health departments and legislative bodies.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, canners argued that children should be employed until midnight.
According to the journal, Jacobi replied cynically that the freshness of the strawberry must be preserved even if the children perish.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, in 1887 he was appointed Chair of the New York State Board of Medical Examiners, and supported written licensure exams.
According to the biographical encyclopedia, Jacobi was widely honored and was twice elected president of the American Pediatric Society.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, he founded and headed the Section on Diseases of Children of the American Medical Association (AMA).
According to an article in PubMed Central, he organized pediatric societies and journals.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, in 1912 he was elected president of the American Medical Association.
According to the website, he was the first physician born outside the United States and the first Jew in the role.
According to the biographical encyclopedia, in 1894 he was invited to the chair of pediatrics at the University of Berlin, and declined, giving as his reason his firm belief in democracy.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, he declined the chair in Berlin out of loyalty to the United States.
Several sources call him the Father of American Pediatrics.
Jacobi Medical Center in New York is named after him.
According to the biographical encyclopedia, in 1873 Jacobi married Mary Putnam.
Of their children, only one daughter, Marjorie, survived to adulthood.
According to the biographical encyclopedia, the fire consumed the records of his life, including diaries, notes and letters.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, he wrote or co-wrote hundreds of scientific papers.
According to the biographical encyclopedia, most of his writings were gathered in the collection Collectanea Jacobi, edited by William Robinson.
According to the AMA Journal of Ethics, critics called his activity socialism.
According to the journal, Jacobi replied that there was no point in claiming that it was socialism or communism.
According to Life in the Fast Lane, there were attempts to expel him and silence him, and he persisted.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, he failed to obtain a patent for the laryngoscope he invented.

claims.quote: Jacobi is widely regarded as the “Father of American Pediatrics.”

claims.text: לפי כתב העת, יעקבי נולד בפרוסיה ב-1831 וברח לאמריקה ב-1853 לאחר מאסר על השתתפותו במהפכות 1848.

claims.quote: In 1860 he was appointed to the first chair of pediatrics at the New York Medical College. There he opened the first free clinic for children.

claims.text: לפי כתב העת, יעקבי היה הראשון שהקים מרפאה חינמית לילדים בארצות הברית.
claims.quote: He was the first to create a free pediatric clinic in the United States

claims.text: לפי האתר, ב-1912 נבחר יעקבי לנשיא איגוד הרופאים האמריקני, הרופא הראשון שנולד מחוץ לארצות הברית והיהודי הראשון בתפקיד.
claims.quote: the first foreign-born and Jewish physician to hold the role

claims.text: לפי האתר, יעקבי היה פרופסור ראשון למחלות ילדים בקולג' הרפואי של ניו יורק ב-1861 והקים את המרפאה הפדיאטרית הראשונה ב-1862.
claims.quote: He was the first professor of childhood diseases at New York Medical College in 1861, established the first pediatric clinic in 1862,

claims.text: לפי האתר, ב-1879 יעקבי הקים בהר סיני את מחלקת האשפוז הפדיאטרית הראשונה בעיר ניו יורק.
claims.quote: Established first inpatient pediatric ward in New York City at Mount Sinai

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה ביוגרפית, יעקבי נולד למשפחה ענייה מאוד בווסטפליה שבגרמניה.
claims.quote: Abraham Jacobi was born into a poverty-stricken family in Westphalia, Germany.

claims.text: לפי האתר, ב-1851 קיבל יעקבי תואר דוקטור לרפואה מאוניברסיטת בון.
claims.quote: 1851 – Received MD from University of Bonn

claims.text: לפי האתר, כסטודנט לרפואה הצטרף יעקבי לליגה הקומוניסטית לצד קרל מרקס וקרל שורץ.
claims.quote: As a medical student, he joined the Communist League alongside figures like Karl Marx and Carl Schurz

claims.text: לפי בריטניקה, יעקבי נאסר בברלין ובקלן בשל השתתפותו בתנועה המהפכנית הגרמנית של 1848.
claims.quote: Because he took part in the German revolutionary movement (1848), Jacobi was imprisoned in

claims.text: לפי האתר, יעקבי נאסר כשנתיים באשמת בגידה בחמורה בשל פעילות מהפכנית.
claims.quote: imprisoned for two years on charges of high treason

claims.text: לפי האתר, אחרי שנתיים בשלשלאות ובבידוד זוכה יעקבי במשפט הקומוניסטים בקלן ב-1852.
claims.quote: After two years in chains and solitary confinement, he was acquitted during the Cologne Communist Trial of 1852

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, יעקבי נאסר אך ברח ב-1853 לארצות הברית.
claims.quote: He was imprisoned but escaped in 1853 to the United States.

claims.text: לפי האתר, ב-1853 היגר יעקבי לארצות הברית ופתח פרקטיקה רפואית בניו יורק.
claims.quote: 1853 – Emigrated to the U.S.; opened medical practice in New York City

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, שנה אחרי בואו לניו יורק המציא יעקבי לרינגוסקופ, אך לא הצליח לרשום עליו פטנט.

claims.text: לפי כתב העת AMA Journal of Ethics, יעקבי ראה ילדים חיים ועובדים בתנאים ירודים ולא בטוחים.
claims.quote: Seeing children living and toiling in substandard and unsafe conditions

claims.text: לפי המאמר, כתבים רפואיים עתיקים עסקו במחלות ילדים רק במסגרת נושאים כלליים.
claims.quote: Medical writings from antiquity did include diseases in children but only in conjunction with general topics.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, בית החולים הנפרד הראשון לילדים נוסד בפילדלפיה ב-1855.
claims.quote: The first separate pediatrics hospital was founded in Philadelphia in 1855.

claims.text: לפי בריטניקה, ב-1860 הפך יעקבי לפרופסור למחלות ילדים בקולג' הרפואי של ניו יורק, בקתדרה הראשונה בנושא שהוקמה בארצות הברית.
claims.quote: became professor of children’s diseases at the New York Medical College in 1860, holding the first chair in the subject founded in the United States.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, יעקבי ארגן את מחלקת הילדים בבית החולים הר סיני בניו יורק.
claims.quote: His activities included the organization of the children's ward at the Mount Sinai Hospital in New York.

claims.text: לפי האתר, יעקבי ארגן מחלקת ילדים במרפאה החיצונית של הר סיני ב-1875 יחד עם אשתו מרי פטנם יעקבי.
claims.quote: by 1875, he and his wife, Mary Putnam Jacobi, MD (1842-1906), had organized a dedicated Children’s Department within its outpatient dispensary.

claims.text: לפי האתר, המחלקה סיפקה טיפול מיוחד בתקופה שבה ילדים טופלו בדרך כלל במחלקות מבוגרים.
claims.quote: This ward provided specialized care in an era when children were commonly treated on adult wards

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, יעקבי היה בין הראשונים שעמדו על הרתחת חלב.
claims.quote: Jacobi was one of the first to insist on the boiling of milk

claims.quote: And he worked to provide pasteurized milk to babies who could not breastfeed

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה יודאיקה, יעקבי היה בין הראשונים שתרגלו החדרת צינור לגרון (אינטובציה) במקום ניתוח קנה (טרכאוטומיה).
claims.quote: one of the first to practice intubation of the throat instead of performing a tracheotomy

claims.quote: In 1870 he returned to the College of Physicians and Surgeons, where he taught for 32 years.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה ביוגרפית, בזמן שרופאים אחרים יעצו לחולי שחפת בשכונות עוני לישון עם הראש על יציאות החירום, יעקבי שאל מדוע יש להשלים עם השכונות הללו.
claims.quote: While other physicians were telling tuberculosis patients in the stifling slums to sleep with their heads resting on the fire escapes, Abraham Jacobi was asking why the slums must be tolerated.

claims.quote: Jacobi believed that improving children’s health required systemic changes in sanitation, housing, nutrition, and education.

claims.quote: Despite attempts to expel and silence him, Jacobi persisted, urging physicians to serve on school boards, health departments, and legislative bodies.

claims.text: לפי כתב העת, בתגובה לטענת יצרני שימורים שיש להעסיק ילדים עד חצות, אמר יעקבי בציניות שיש לשמר את טריות התות גם אם הילדים יאבדו.
claims.quote: The freshness of the strawberry must be preserved even if the children perish.

claims.text: לפי האתר, ב-1887 מונה יעקבי ליו"ר מועצת הבוחנים הרפואיים של מדינת ניו יורק ותמך בבחינות רישוי כתובות.

claims.quote: Declined prestigious professorship in Berlin out of loyalty to the U.S.

claims.quote: It is useless to call that socialism or communism.

claims.quote: Appointed Professor of Infantile Pathology and Therapeutics, New York Medical College
